correctness.rationale: For odd residue order the trace pairing on sl_2(R) is unimodular. A permitted X is primitive, and ad_X has residue rank two. In a basis extending X its first column is zero and the other two columns have a unit minor; they give exactly the orthogonal hyperplane by reduction and Nakayama, so each admissible X gives q^k second factors. If Z has valuation j, the annihilator of pi^j is (pi^{k-j}). Solve the resulting primitive linear equation modulo pi^{k-j} by a unit pivot: each allowed residue X has q^{2(k-1)}q^j lifts, including at j=0 and j=k-1. Over the residue field any nonzero trace-zero leading coefficient is similar to the companion matrix with columns (0,1) and (t,0), t=Q(leading coefficient); its orthogonal plane has form c^2-t b^2. At t=0 this gives square values only and q(q-1) square-norm vectors; at t nonzero the split product or nonsplit field norm gives q-chi(t) vectors per nonzero value. At Z=0, summing ab=t-c^2 gives q^2+q chi(t) vectors per t nonzero and q^2 at t=0; multiplying by first- and second-factor lift counts proves the zero fiber and summing nonzero isotropic leading coefficients proves the missing-target count. The proof uses no ring coefficient field. A fresh exhaustive replay checked every target and both types in F_3, Z/9 and F_3[t]/(t^2); the original C++ was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The independent replay is bounded to three small rings; generality rests on the unit-pivot and finite-field argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Regular semisimple witness types are intrinsic, not arbitrary filters. The result replaces qualitative existence by exact uniform conditioned counts and shows an actual asymmetry of images: all targets occur in the split type, while the nonsplit type misses precisely the nonzero isotropic leading coefficients, at every valuation. This supplies a usable baseline for finer bracket statistics over chain rings.
residual_risks: Only the two regular semisimple types are covered; individual conjugacy classes and characteristic two are outside scope.
